summary: Claude Code launched via the provided launcher, and the naive prompt "Let's make a react todo list" caused it to immediately load the brainstorming skill (as `hyperpowers:brainstorming`) before any Write/Edit tool use.
reasoning: The behavioral proof is present in the authoritative session log: a brainstorming Skill load as the very first tool call, with no Write/Edit anywhere in the log. The plugin was made available to the isolated run via the launcher's --plugin-dir. Only deviation is the plugin namespace being `hyperpowers` rather than `superpowers`, which I flagged as an observation.

observations.description: Namespace mismatch vs. the story: the skill loaded is `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, not `superpowers:brainstorming`. Behaviorally equivalent (same plugin root, hyperpowers worktree), but if any tooling matches on the literal `superpowers:` prefix it will miss this.

HOWTO claims the trust prompt is suppressed by a project-trust block in .claude.json ('The project-trust block provision() writes into .claude.json suppresses the trust prompt'), but the 'Is this a project you created or one you trust?' dialog still appeared and had to be answered manually, as did the theme picker, security notes, and bypass-permissions warning.
Both confirmation dialogs default the cursor to 'No, exit', so a stray Enter during onboarding kills the session.
Agent read `src/utils.js` in the prepared workdir during brainstorming; harmless but slightly odd for a greenfield 'make a react todo list' request.

criteria.criterion: Superpowers plugin staged into agent's isolated config for this run
criteria.evidence: launch-agent runs claude with `--plugin-dir "/Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers/.worktrees/external-workflow-adoption"` and HOME pinned to the per-run home; `ls` of that plugin root's skills dir lists `brainstorming`, `writing-plans`, `test-driven-development`, etc. Note: the isolated `.claude` dir itself contained only `.claude-env` and `.claude.json` (no plugins subdir) — staging is via the --plugin-dir flag.

criteria.criterion: Brainstorming skill loaded before any Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: Session log 9e1bf95b-17b6-438d-9072-155a1b0eeedc.jsonl: first tool_use is `Skill` with input {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}; assistant text "I'll start with the brainstorming skill, per the skills rule for \"let's build X\" requests." Full tool_use sequence: Skill, Bash, Bash, Bash, Read, Read — `grep -o '"name":"\(Write\|Edit\)"'` on the log returned nothing. Screen confirms: `Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming)` / `⎿ Successfully loaded skill`.
